land.text: Laos, 'finally established a sovereign, independent Laos' by the Franco-Lao Treaty of 22 October 1953

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps Laos inside French Indochina to 1955 and starts this row in 1956. The page dates the unification of the kingdom to 11 May 1947, within the French Union.

successors.note: Cliopatria starts Communist Laos in January 1976; the Pathet Lao took the capital on 23 August 1975 and the republic dates from 2 December 1975 (the infobox gives the takeover as 23 August 1975).

correction.text: Laos from the Franco-Lao Treaty of 22 October 1953; Phongsali and Houaphan held by the Pathet Lao

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws Laos inside French Indochina to 1955. The page gives 'its independence on 22 October 1953' and 'unification 11 May 1947'; no boundary, so the 1956 outline is borrowed.

229,137 km2 for 1956-1966 against the infobox 236,800 km2 (ratio 0.97). The outline matches modern Laos except that it takes about 2,300 km2 across the Mekong in Thailand and misses 35 cells (8,900 km2) of Laos along the Thai border. Phongsali and Houaphan (Xam Neua) stay in the shape although the Pathet Lao held them (contest events below).

correction.text: the whole of the Kingdom as in 1956-1966; the south-eastern border strip is PAVN-occupied, not lost

keyframe_review.note: 216,315 km2 for 1967-1972: Cliopatria cuts about 10,600 km2 from Xekong, Attapu, Savannakhet and Saravan along the Vietnamese border in 1967. The Kingdom page says 'North Vietnam invaded and occupied parts of Laos as a supply route'; the Civil War page dates the seizure of Attapeu to 1 May 1970 and the Bolaven Plateau to 1971, and nothing to 1967. The sovereign claim is kept and the strip is a hatched occupation by the DRV (rule 4).

correction.text: the whole of the Kingdom as in 1956-1966, with the Vietnamese-occupied strip and the Pathet Lao provinces as events

keyframe_review.note: 216,168 km2 for 1973-1975: the 1967 outline with two cells swapped. Cliopatria's Democratic Republic of Vietnam shape of 1973 includes 37 Laotian cells (11,400 km2) of the same strip. The ceasefire came 'in February 1973 following the Paris Peace Accords' and a Provisional Government of National Unity under Souvanna Phouma in April 1974; the page gives no line of division, so the occupation events continue to 1975.

region.text: Laos, a sovereign, independent kingdom under the Franco-Lao Treaty

ledger.note: 1953: the Kingdom of Laos becomes independent (22 October). 'The country was governed as a constitutional monarchy beginning with its independence on 22 October 1953'; the page names no boundary, so the region is Cliopatria's 1956 outline.

region.text: the border provinces of Phongsali and Xam Neua (Houaphan), conquered by the PAVN in April 1953 and left to the Pathet Lao to occupy

ledger.note: 1953: the north-east is in rebel hands from the start. In April 1953 the PAVN 'conquered the border provinces of Phongsali and Xam Neua' and 'moved aside' for the Pathet Lao; Souphanouvong's headquarters moved into Xam Neua on 19 April; royal troops were sent to the two provinces in 1955.

region.text: the border provinces of Phongsali and Xam Neua (Houaphan), conquered by the PAVN in April 1953 and left to the Pathet Lao to occupy

ledger.note: 1957: the Pathet Lao enters the government. 'In November, 1957, a coalition government incorporating the Pathet Lao was finally established'; the page dates the integration of 1,500 Pathet Lao troops to May 1959.

region.text: the border provinces of Phongsali and Xam Neua (Houaphan), conquered by the PAVN in April 1953 and left to the Pathet Lao to occupy

ledger.note: 1959: the civil war begins (infobox 23 May 1959): two Pathet Lao battalions escape integration; 'On 28 July, PAVN units attacked all along the North Vietnamese-Lao border'. The page names no provinces held in 1960-1962.

region.text: Xiangkhoang Province and the Plain of Jars: on 1 January 1961 a communist coalition drove 9,000 Royal Lao Army troops from the Plain; recovered in September 1969, lost again in February 1970, fought over to 1972

ledger.note: 1961: the Plain of Jars falls. On 1 January 1961 a communist coalition drove 9,000 Royal Lao Army troops from the Plain of Jars; the Royal army retook it in September 1969 (Kou Kiet), lost it on 11-25 February 1970 when it abandoned Xieng Khoang city, and fought for it in Campaign Z (18 December 1971) and from 21 May 1972.

region.text: the south-eastern border strip (Xekong, Attapu, eastern Savannakhet and Saravan; about 10,600 km2) that Cliopatria cuts from the Kingdom's shape in 1967; 'North Vietnam invaded and occupied parts of Laos as a supply route' (the Ho Chi Minh Trail)

ledger.note: 1967: the Ho Chi Minh Trail strip leaves the Kingdom's shape in Cliopatria. The pages are silent on the year; the Kingdom page says only 'North Vietnam invaded and occupied parts of Laos as a supply route', so the year is Cliopatria's and the confidence 1.

region.text: Attapeu, seized on 1 May 1970 by PAVN units joined with the Pathet Lao

ledger.note: 1970: PAVN and the Pathet Lao seize Attapeu (1 May): 'PAVN units (28th and 24A regiments) joined the NVA and Pathet Lao to seize Attapeu'.

region.text: the Bolaven Plateau, captured in 1971 by Pathet Lao and PAVN forces; the 60 km circle is the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1971: the Bolaven Plateau falls. 'In 1971, Pathet Lao and PAVN forces reclaimed the Tha Teng and Lao Nam areas and captured the Bolaven Plateau'.

region.text: the border provinces of Phongsali and Xam Neua (Houaphan), conquered by the PAVN in April 1953 and left to the Pathet Lao to occupy

ledger.note: 1975: the monarchy ends and the Pathet Lao rules the whole country (2 December). Pathet Lao troops arrived at Savannakhet on 31 May, occupied Luang Phrabang in early June and took Vientiane on 23 August.

region.text: Xiangkhoang Province and the Plain of Jars: on 1 January 1961 a communist coalition drove 9,000 Royal Lao Army troops from the Plain; recovered in September 1969, lost again in February 1970, fought over to 1972

ledger.note: 1975: the Plain of Jars passes to the Pathet Lao with the rest of the country (2 December).

region.text: the south-eastern border strip (Xekong, Attapu, eastern Savannakhet and Saravan; about 10,600 km2) that Cliopatria cuts from the Kingdom's shape in 1967; 'North Vietnam invaded and occupied parts of Laos as a supply route' (the Ho Chi Minh Trail)

ledger.note: 1975: the strip ends as Vietnamese-occupied land when the Pathet Lao takes the state (2 December); the Pathet Lao and Hanoi remained allied.

ledger.note: 1975: Attapeu passes to the Pathet Lao state (2 December).

region.text: the Bolaven Plateau, captured in 1971 by Pathet Lao and PAVN forces; the 60 km circle is the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1975: the Bolaven Plateau passes to the Pathet Lao state (2 December).

1975: the Kingdom ends (2 December): 'It survived until 2 December 1975'. Prince Vong Savang submitted the king's letter of abdication to the Pathet Lao; the Lao People's Democratic Republic was established with Souphanouvong as President.

wars.outcome: Pathet Lao and North Vietnamese victory: the Kingdom of Laos ended and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed on 2 December 1975.
wars.note: Infobox 23 May 1959 to 2 December 1975. The 1962 International Agreement on the Neutrality of Laos (Geneva, 23 July 1962) led to a coalition of the Royal Lao Government, the Pathet Lao and Kong Le's neutralists; the Vietnamese communists repatriated 'only a token 40 technicians out of an estimated 2,000'. Ceasefire in February 1973.

certainty.note: Colonial-era frontiers inherited from French Indochina; Phongsali and Houaphan were held by the Pathet Lao without a recorded line.
The Plain of Jars changed hands from 1961 to 1972 and the south-eastern strip was held by PAVN without a recorded line.

notes: Page budget (1-2) spent on the Kingdom article and the Civil War article. Cliopatria's 1967 shape cuts a 10,600 km2 strip along the Vietnamese border (Xekong, Attapu, Savannakhet, Saravan) that does not appear in any other row until 1973, when the Democratic Republic of Vietnam shape takes 37 Laotian cells; the dossier keeps the sovereign claim and carries the strip as a hatched occupation by the DRV. The Kingdom's start date is its independence (22 October 1953); the page also gives 11 May 1947 as the unification of the kingdom within the French Union, and the Thai-held Sayaboury and Champasak of 1941-1946 are in the kingdom-of-thailand dossier (counterpart french-indochina). The 1956 outline takes 2,300 km2 of Thailand and omits 8,900 km2 of Laos on the Thai border: a Cliopatria quirk, not corrected. The Pathet Lao is written here as a rebel state (slug pathet-lao); the pages give no percentage of land held by it in any year, so only Phongsali, Houaphan and the Plain of Jars are drawn. The page's infobox gives the Communist takeover as 23 August 1975 and the text 2 December 1975; this dossier ends on 2 December. Not on the pages: the Vientiane Agreement of 21 February 1973 (only 'a ceasefire in February 1973'), the 1954 Geneva regroupment provinces, the Ho Chi Minh Trail by name on the Kingdom page. Gazetteer name needed: Bolaven Plateau (region, Champasak-Attapeu-Xekong, about 106.3 E 15.1 N).
